doc.title: Michael Max Fleming interviewed by Monk Rowe, New Hartford, New York, June 8, 2017

title: Hardships, Freddie Cole, and playing with the greats
summary: He describes lean times in New York, good treatment with Freddie Cole, and being called by Bill Evans, Kenny Barron, Horace Silver and Art Farmer.

story.theme_name: Making a living: hard times, day jobs and scarce work
story.community_name: Day jobs: musicians working outside music

blocks.x: Well I look at it as I was destined to. I don’t understand it. For me, like I say, I wasn’t bragging when I said that I never had a real day gig or like that. I’m overwhelmingly humbled by, hey, I got to do what I want to do, man. You know. Look, I can’t think of anything greater. I mean it hasn’t been easy. There was times when I was saying, “Which bank am I going to rob.” No I’m dramatizing, but I’m saying there were times when I lived in a room a fourth the size of this room we’re in now. I had to walk up four flights of steps with my bass, have to get up, after 4:30 in the morning playing a gig, move my car at 8. Oh that’s been in New York City, come on man. It’s not all peaches and cream you know. There’s been times. One time a guy didn’t like my behavior. “You know guys like you get a surprise. Maybe something like throw him through this window.” Or you’re walking down the street and you get run over. “You’re a wise guy, huh?” I’ve been through all kinds of stuff. You know what I mean? All kinds of stuff. I worked with Freddie Cole, Nat Cole’s brother. The best of everything. The best of everything. Anything on the menu. Lobster, steak, anything. We never came through the back door. Never. Then those other guys who are standing in the kitchen dripping, eating a sandwich. You know. And you’ve got to come up through the back elevator. So there’s a lot to the music. But the good thing is I’ve been able to meet all kinds of people. All kinds of people. Just a wonderful thing. All kinds of musicians. And for me the greatest thing that’s ever happened to me is that I’ve been able to play with the greats. Bill Evans. Kenny Barron. You know I’ve had a lot of people call me that I couldn’t go work with. Horace Silver, Art Farmer, just hear their voices on the phone.
So it’s been good to me.
